Have a schedule, have a routine, have a calender, have goals. All very different things that feed into each other.

Your goals should shape your calendar, your calendar should shape your schedule, your schedule should shape your daily routine. Write everything out and when you see it all come together it should become the guide for your day.

Goals - what is it you want to accomplish in 3-5 years? what do you want to accomplish this year to achieve that bigger goal? what do you want to accomplish this month? what do you want to accomplish this week? what do you want to accomplish today?

Example: Home ownership in three years. This year I will save $2K for a down payment. I need to cut $166 from our monthly expenses to put into savings. That means I need to cut down our food budget by $30 a month, our utilities by $20 a months, our clothing budget by $25, and our entertainment by $50, and I still need to find an additional $41 in savings

A calendar - what events and commentments are coming up this week/month? This will help you see what's coming and prepare for it better

Example: The kids have a Christmas pagent they need costumes for, the Smiths want to meet up for dinner, and it's my sister's birthday. Also, prepping 20 homemade from scratch dinners to save on groceries, and researching cheaper phone plans

A schedule - what projects do you have to get done this week? What can you do today to move it along? Set them out and then estimate prep time, down time, etc. After thinking about your routine, try to assign a specific time in your day to do each thing

Example: To save $$ instead of buying a costume for the pagent I will repurpose something. It's going to take about three hours. I also have to grate my block of cheese for dinner prep for the week, call the Smiths and invite them to dinner instead of going out (they usually are home around 4pm, I'll call then), and search for coupons online for my sisters presants. I also need to call our phone company

A routine - an order of operations to perform tasks. Find a routine that works for you, especially around chores. It becomes automatic and less burdensome. Also it will allow you reliable blocks of time to work on projects and errands surrounding project

Example: After breakfast the kids watch two episodes of their favorite cartoon. That gives me 45 minutes to work on one of my projects - grating cheese, working on costume, etc

Write them down and review them. All the little things you do should be contributing to the things you have written down as uoir big family goals. It helps order your day
